newsitem.title: USA: Miami to vote on dissolution plan - election chief.
newsitem.headline: Miami to vote on dissolution plan - election chief.

text.p: Election supervisors certified petitions Tuesday calling for the dissolution of City of Miami, a move that will force an election on the proposal within 240 days.
Petition signatures were collected by a group called Citizens for Lower Taxes, which wants the fiscally troubled city to be dissolved and absorbed into the Dade County government.
County Election Supervisor David Leahy said a random sampling of 100 voter signatures proved the petitions were valid. Proponents collected 20,247 signatures, far more than needed to force the vote.

"The city would have 120 days to then draft a (ballot) proposal," Leahy said. "Once that proposal is drafted, then the clock starts ticking again. At that point they have 120 days to conduct the election."

Miami is struggling to close a $68 million deficit in its $275 million budget for the year that began October 1. Its bond ratings have been cut to non-investment grade, and the city has been placed under supervision of a state oversight board.

The fiscal problems came to light after three top city officials resigned last fall to face federal corruption charges. Attorney Gene Stearns, one of the leaders of the dissolution movement, said the fiscal problems prove Miami officials are incapable of governing.

He said surrounding cities have also been hurt by Miami's battered reputation. Miami is one of 29 separate cities that make up the Miami metropolitan area that sprawls across Dade County. Two-thirds of those with "Miami" in their mailing addresses don't live within even live within the city limits, Stearns said.
"The fact is, the City of Miami gives Miami a bad name," Stearns said.

Stearns' group has calculated that the average Miami homeowner would pay $612 a year less in taxes if the city is absorbed into the Metro-Dade government. Mayor Joe Carollo disputed that, putting the savings at only $230 a year.
